newsitem.title: UK: Britain elects first Moslem MP.
newsitem.headline: Britain elects first Moslem MP.

text.p: Britons elected their first Moslem member of parliament on Friday as the Labour Party swept to a landslide victory.
Pakistan-born Mohammed Sarwar, a millionaire businessman, was elected as Labour's MP for the seat of Govan in Glasgow with a comfortable majority.
But Sarwar was not on stage when the result was read out because he and seven other candidates for the seat refused to stand alongside the extreme-right British National Party's (BNP) candidate.
The BNP campaigns for an end to immigration and the repatriation of non-whites. Anti-racist groups have linked it to several racial attacks in Britain.

Sarwar, who was born near Faisalabad, has said he hopes his election will give a greater voice to Britain's ethnic communities. "This is a great day for the people of Govan and the people of Scotland," he said in his acceptance speech.
